headline: Benin shows how nations can deliver on climate goals
meta_description: Benin doubled drinking water access in five years and created 25,000 jobs through smart domestic funding, proving SDG progress is possible with four years left.
summary_short: West African nation Benin has doubled access to clean drinking water in five years and created 25,000 jobs by increasing domestic revenue and issuing Africa's first SDG…
body:
With less than four years until the 2030 deadline for the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, Benin is offering a rare bright spot: concrete proof that transformation happens when governments prioritize funding and follow through. Over the past decade, the West African nation has increased its domestic revenue by 0.5 per cent of GDP each year. In 2021, it issued Africa's first SDG bond—a financial tool that channeled money directly into expanding access to education and drinking water. The results speak for themselves. Access to drinking water has jumped from 40 per cent to 80 per cent in just five years. A new industrial zone launched the same year has created 25,000 jobs.

Benin's minister of economic cooperation, Aristide Medenou, stressed a simple truth at the UN's annual SDG Moment event: "If a country is not able to increase the domestic revenue, the country cannot go forward in implementing the SDGs." It's a lesson emerging as the world confronts a sobering reality. Only 36 per cent of the 139 tracked targets are on track or making moderate progress. Food insecurity affects 2.1 billion people, and a $4 trillion annual financing gap threatens decades of work.

Yet the past decade has delivered measurable wins across the globe. Nearly a billion people have gained access to safely managed drinking water. Internet access has expanded from 40 per cent to 74 per cent of the world's population. Electricity now reaches 92 per cent of people worldwide. UN Secretary-General António Guterres reminded world leaders that "progress was never automatic. It was earned through the determination of people, communities and countries." Young leaders at the event, including Suzuka Nakamura of Japan, called on governments to move with the same urgency that defined the goals' adoption eleven years ago. "There is still time to act," she said, "but we need to move together."
quick_facts: Benin doubled drinking water access from 40% to 80% in five years
Africa's first SDG bond issued in 2021 created 25,000 jobs
Nearly one billion people gained access to safe drinking water since 2015
Only 36% of tracked development targets are on track or making progress
Four years remain until the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline
